items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the highway law and the transportation corporations law, in
relation to the department of transportation not requiring surveying in
certain situations
items.lawCode: Amd §10, Hway L; amd §7, Transp Corps L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8472             Revised 3/7/2022

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the highway law and the transportation corporations law,
in relation to the department of transportation not requiring surveying
in certain situations

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation will limit the department of transportation's ability
to require surveying in certain situations.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Amends section 10 of the Highway law to specify when surveys
are required as part of the application for use and occupancy of a state
department of transportation right of way for the purposes of install-
ing, modifying, relocating, repairing, operating, or maintaining fiber
optic facilities.

Section 2. Amends section 7 of the transportation corporations law, as
added by section 2 of part RRR of chapter 59 of the laws of 2019 by
adding a new part, to state that a survey the department of transporta-
tion shall not require a survey for the purposes of installing, modify-
ing, relocating, repairing, operating, or maintaining fiber optic facil-
ities as part of the department of transportation's consolidated
application, when such use and occupancy of the state right of way is
utilizing existing infrastructure, including but not limited to aerial
pole attachments and underground conduits.

Section 3. Effective Date

 
JUSTIFICATION:

During the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, access to internet service
became absolutely essential for to facilitate the ability for individ-
uals to work remotely, attend school remotely and connect with others.
However, the COVID-19 pandemic also exposed the true extent of the
digital divide in New York State, which has shown the need to rapidly
deploy access to broadband and fiberoptic utilities.

However, several actions that have been taken by the State since 2019
has caused a significantly backlog and slowing of the ability to deploy
this vital resource across the state. Specifically, in 2020 the Depart-
ment of Transportation added a new requirement as part of the expanded
consolidated application for the deployment of fiberoptic utilities.
This new requirement requires surveys to conducted on the state's own
right-of-way, which has added significant expense and time to the
deployment process. This legislation seeks to streamline this process to
not require a survey when the proposed deployment will be utilizing
existing pole attachment or conduit that exists in the state's right of
way and thereby will facilitate a more rapid deployment.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately
